about.title: About Lukotta
about.description: Lukotta is a free, open-source macOS app that opens BitLocker, NTFS and Linux drives. Written by Clement Rahula under the GNU General Public License.
about.lead: Lukotta opens drives and disk images that macOS cannot read. It is free, open source, and maintained by one person.

sections.heading: What it is
paragraphs: Lukotta is a macOS application. It opens BitLocker, NTFS, LUKS, ext4, btrfs and XFS drives, and virtual machine disk images in the qcow2, VMDK, VDI, VHD and VHDX formats. macOS cannot read any of those on its own. It can read NTFS but not write to it.

It starts a small Linux virtual machine in the background, opens the drive there, and hands it back to Finder. Linux has read these formats for years. The drive is not converted or copied. It stays as it was, and the machine it came from still reads it.

sections.heading: Who maintains it
paragraphs: [A single developer](https://rahula.dev). There is no company, no investors and no team.

sections.heading: Why it exists
paragraphs: Plug a BitLocker drive into a Mac and Finder offers to erase it. It does not ask for a password, and nothing on screen shows that the drive is locked rather than broken.
It seemed silly that in this day and age there is no practical way to share an encrypted USB drive between multiple operating systems, so a solution had to be developed.
The Linux ecosystem already had tools that could read those drives. Lukotta puts that together with a Mac interface.

sections.heading: What it costs
paragraphs: Nothing. There is no paid version, no subscription, no trial and no account.
Lukotta is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. The source is published. Anyone may read it, change it and pass it on under the same licence.

sections.heading: Nothing leaves your Mac
paragraphs: Lukotta has no analytics, no telemetry and no crash reporting.
It makes one kind of network request: it checks for updates and downloads one if you ask. Passwords and recovery keys are used to unlock the drive and are not stored, sent or logged.

sections.heading: Source code
paragraphs: The application source code is at github.com/clementrahula/lukotta.

contact.title: Contact
contact.description: How to report a bug in Lukotta, ask a question, or report a security problem. Issues on GitHub are read first and usually answered fastest.
contact.lead: Bugs go to GitHub. Security problems go to the address in SECURITY.md. Everything else goes to email.

sections.heading: A bug, or a drive that will not open
paragraphs: Open an issue at github.com/clementrahula/lukotta/issues. Issues are read first, and they are public, so the next person with the same drive can find the answer.
Say what the drive is, what Lukotta showed you, and what you expected. Quote any error exactly. Do not paste a password or a recovery key into an issue.

sections.heading: A security problem
paragraphs: Do not open a public issue. SECURITY.md in the repository says where to send it and what to expect.

sections.heading: Anything else
paragraphs: Email contact_web@lukotta.com with questions about the app.

sections.heading: How long a reply takes
paragraphs: Lukotta is maintained by one person. There is no support desk and no promised response time. Some messages take a while, and some go unanswered.
A GitHub issue is usually faster, because someone else may answer first.
